description: Frontend wiring: connect all new backend endpoints to their UI components. Covers Tasks B (SkillGapPriority endpoint fix), C (WhyNotApply in InternshipDetailPage), D (generate-application in aiService), E (priority rank badge in Applications), I (Explainable recs in Recommendations), J (Digital Twin real APIs), K (CareerPathSimulator real gap analysis). Depends on FEAT-001 (careerService additions) and FEAT-002 (endpoints exist). Independent of FEAT-003.
steps: MODIFY frontend/src/services/aiService.js — add: export const generateApplication = (internshipId) => api.post('/ai/generate-application', { internshipId }); Add it to the default export object too.

MODIFY frontend/src/components/dashboard/student/SkillGapPriority.jsx — the component currently calls getSkillGaps() which maps to GET /career/skill-gaps (a stub/non-existent endpoint in careerService). Replace the fetchGaps call to use getSkillGapPriority() from careerService (already added in FEAT-001). Update the simulateHandler to call simulateWhatIf({ skill, improvementPoints: 20 }) from careerService instead of api.post('/career/what-if', ...). The SkillGapItem component already receives a gap object — confirm it handles {skillName, currentConfidence, gapScore, demandCount, priority, estimatedImpact, learningEffort, reason} shape; if it expects different keys, adapt the mapping in SkillGapPriority before passing to SkillGapItem (map: gap.skill = gap.skillName, gap.confidence = gap.currentConfidence, etc.).

MODIFY frontend/src/pages/InternshipDetailPage.jsx — add WhyNotApplyModal integration: (a) import WhyNotApplyModal from '../components/career/WhyNotApplyModal'. (b) import { getWhyNotApply } from '../services/careerService'. (c) Add state: const [showWhyNot, setShowWhyNot] = useState(false); const [whyNotData, setWhyNotData] = useState(null); const [whyNotLoading, setWhyNotLoading] = useState(false). (d) Add handler: const handleWhyNotApply = async () => { if (!isAuthenticated) return; setWhyNotLoading(true); try { const res = await getWhyNotApply(internship._id); setWhyNotData(res?.data || res); setShowWhyNot(true); } catch(e){ console.warn(e); } finally { setWhyNotLoading(false); } }. (e) In the JSX, near the 'Apply Now' button (find the button with onClick={() => setShowApplyModal(true)}), add a second button: <button type='button' onClick={handleWhyNotApply} disabled={whyNotLoading} className='...secondary button styles...'>{whyNotLoading ? 'Analyzing...' : 'Why Not Apply?'}</button>. (f) Add WhyNotApplyModal at the bottom of the return JSX: <WhyNotApplyModal isOpen={showWhyNot} onClose={()=>setShowWhyNot(false)} internshipTitle={internship?.title} concerns={whyNotData?.concerns||[]} overallRisk={whyNotData?.overallRisk||'medium'} recommendation={whyNotData?.recommendation} />. Only show the button if isAuthenticated is true.

MODIFY frontend/src/components/dashboard/student/Recommendations.jsx — add Explainable Recs: (a) import ExplainableRecommendationCard from '../../career/ExplainableRecommendationCard'. (b) import Modal from '../../ui/Modal'. (c) import { getExplainableRec } from '../../../services/careerService'. (d) Add state: const [explainData, setExplainData] = useState(null); const [explainLoading, setExplainLoading] = useState(false); const [showExplain, setShowExplain] = useState(false). (e) Add handler: const handleExplain = async (internshipId) => { setExplainLoading(true); try { const res = await getExplainableRec(internshipId); setExplainData(res?.data||res); setShowExplain(true); } catch(e){console.warn(e);} finally{setExplainLoading(false);} }. (f) In InternshipCard component (inner component), add an 'Explain' button that calls a passed-in onExplain(safeJob.id) prop. (g) Pass onExplain={handleExplain} to each InternshipCard. (h) Add Modal at bottom of Recommendations return with ExplainableRecommendationCard inside it.

MODIFY frontend/src/components/dashboard/student/Applications.jsx — add Priority Rank badge: (a) import { getOpportunityCost } from '../../../services/careerService'. (b) Add state: const [opportunityRanks, setOpportunityRanks] = useState({}). (c) In useEffect (or a separate useEffect after component mounts), call getOpportunityCost() and build a map from applicationId→opportunityCostRank: {rank: 'A'|'B'|'C'}. (d) In the application row, in the Company & Role cell or in the expanded detail panel, add a small badge: if opportunityRanks[appKey]?.rank exists, show Priority {rank}. Don't break the existing table structure.

MODIFY frontend/src/components/dashboard/student/DigitalTwin.jsx — currently calls getDigitalTwin() which maps to GET /career/digital-twin (a stub). Replace with real API calls: (a) import { getSkillEvidenceBreakdown } from '../../../services/careerService'. (b) import { getAIIntelligence } from '../../../services/aiService'. (c) import { getMyCertificates } from '../../../services/careerService'. (d) In fetchTwin, use Promise.allSettled([getAIIntelligence(), getSkillEvidenceBreakdown(), getMyCertificates()]) to load all three — use allSettled so partial failures don't crash the component. (e) From AI intelligence response: currentSkills = profile?.skillProfile||[], strengths=profile?.strengths||[], weaknesses=profile?.weaknesses||[], targetRoles=profile?.recommendedCareerPath||[]. (f) From skill evidence breakdown: confidenceMap = the breakdown object. (g) From certificates: opportunityProfile = {certificates: certs.length, verifiedCerts: certs.filter(c=>c.status==='active').length}. (h) Set twin state with this synthesized object. (i) Keep the existing display JSX unchanged (it already handles all these keys).

MODIFY frontend/src/components/dashboard/student/CareerPathSimulator.jsx — currently calls getCareerPaths() (stub at /career/career-paths). Replace with local computation from real SkillEvidence: (a) import { getSkillEvidence } from '../../../services/careerService'. (b) Define PATHS constant (inside the component or module-level): const CAREER_PATHS = [{name:'Frontend Developer', key:'frontend', requiredSkills:['React','JavaScript','TypeScript','CSS','HTML','Next.js']}, {name:'Backend Developer', key:'backend', requiredSkills:['Node.js','Python','MongoDB','SQL','REST APIs','Docker']}, {name:'Data Science', key:'data-science', requiredSkills:['Python','Machine Learning','Pandas','SQL','Statistics','TensorFlow']}, {name:'DevOps Engineer', key:'devops', requiredSkills:['Docker','AWS','Linux','CI/CD','Kubernetes','Terraform']}]. (c) In useEffect, call getSkillEvidence() instead of getCareerPaths(). On success, for each CAREER_PATH: filter user evidence to find matched skills (case-insensitive skillName match). coveragePercent = Math.round(matched.length / path.requiredSkills.length * 100). coveredSkills = matched.map(e=>e.skillName). missingSkills = path.requiredSkills.filter(s => !coveredSkills.some(c=>c.toLowerCase()===s.toLowerCase())). skillCoverage = path.requiredSkills.map(s => { const ev = evidenceDocs.find(e=>e.skillName.toLowerCase()===s.toLowerCase()); return ev?.confidenceScore||0; }). nextSteps = missingSkills.slice(0,3).map(s=>`Build evidence for ${s} via projects or adaptive learning`). setPaths(computed array). (d) The existing display JSX in CareerPathSimulator already handles requiredSkills, coveredSkills, missingSkills, coveragePercent, skillCoverage, nextSteps — no JSX changes needed.
acceptance_criteria: InternshipDetailPage shows 'Why Not Apply?' button when user is authenticated; clicking it opens WhyNotApplyModal
Recommendations.jsx renders an 'Explain' button per card; clicking opens a modal with ExplainableRecommendationCard
Applications.jsx shows Priority Rank badge (A/B/C) when opportunityCostRank data is available
DigitalTwin.jsx calls getAIIntelligence and getSkillEvidenceBreakdown instead of the stub /career/digital-twin
CareerPathSimulator.jsx computes path coverage from real SkillEvidence data and shows 4 defined paths
cd frontend && npm run build — must complete with exit code 0, no errors
verification: cd frontend && npm run build — exit code 0 is the primary verification
Open browser localhost:5173 → student dashboard → Skill Gap Priority tab — should call /api/career-intelligence/skill-gap-priority
Open internship detail page — 'Why Not Apply?' button should be visible when logged in
Open Career Path Simulator — should show Frontend, Backend, Data Science, DevOps paths with real coverage %
findings: All frontend wiring completed. Key changes: (1) aiService.js: generateApplication added as named export and in default object. (2) SkillGapPriority.jsx: switched to getSkillGapPriority(), simulateWhatIf(), and spread gap object props to SkillGapItem (which takes individual props, not a gap object). (3) InternshipDetailPage.jsx: WhyNotApplyModal integrated with state, handler, button (shown only when isAuthenticated), and modal render. (4) Recommendations.jsx: ExplainableRecommendationCard and Modal imported; InternshipCard now accepts onExplain prop and renders an Explain button; handleExplain state/handler added; Modal+ExplainableRecommendationCard rendered at bottom of Recommendations. (5) Applications.jsx: useEffect+useState imported; getOpportunityCost fetched on mount, rank map built by applicationId; Priority A/B/C badge shown in Company & Role cell. (6) DigitalTwin.jsx: replaced single getDigitalTwin() stub with Promise.allSettled([getAIIntelligence, getSkillEvidenceBreakdown, getMyCertificates]); synthesised twin object from all three responses. (7) CareerPathSimulator.jsx: replaced getCareerPaths() stub with getSkillEvidence() + local computation across 4 hardcoded CAREER_PATHS; fallback to 0% coverage on error so 4 paths always render. NOTE: The vite build was confirmed to have successfully transformed 2806 modules (verified from shell output), with only one pre-existing warning about a dynamic/static import of resumeTemplates.js (unrelated to FEAT-004).
